Let $\mathsf U,\mathsf V$ be probability laws on the same finite space with $\mathsf U\le A\mathsf V$, $A\ge1$, and let $C$ be a finite observation. For $0<\eta<1$, $$\mathsf U_C\{c:\mathsf U_C(c)<\eta\mathsf V_C(c)\}\le\eta.
 \label{eq:conditioning-likelihood}$$ At every other $\mathsf U_C$-positive value, $$\mathsf U(\,\cdot\mid C=c)
 \le \frac A\eta\,\mathsf V(\,\cdot\mid C=c).$$ The estimate is independent of the number of values of $C$.*


*In particular, let $\mathsf P$ be a finite law, let $\mathcal E$ have mass $m=\mathsf P(\mathcal E)>0$, and put $\mathsf U=\mathsf P(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal E)$ and $r_C(c)=\mathsf P(\mathcal E\mid C=c)$. Then $$\begin{gathered}
 \mathsf U_C(c)=\frac{\mathsf P_C(c)r_C(c)}m,\qquad
 \mathsf U_C\{r_C<t\}\le\frac tm\quad(t>0),\\
 \mathsf U(\,\cdot\mid C=c)
 \le r_C(c)^{-1}\mathsf P(\,\cdot\mid C=c).
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:retention-fibers}$$ The last inequality is asserted on positive $\mathsf U_C$ fibers. Thus for $0<\eta_0<1$, outside $\mathsf U_C$-mass $\eta_0$, their domination constants are at most $(m\eta_0)^{-1}$.*




*Suppose further that $C$ is a function of a finite parent observation $X$, and write $r_X(x)=\mathsf P(\mathcal E\mid X=x)$. On every positive $C=c$ fiber, for $0<\eta_1<1$, $$\mathsf U\{r_X(X)<\eta_1r_C(c)\mid C=c\}\le\eta_1.
 \label{eq:nested-retention-fibers}$$ Removing these parent values does not change a conditional law given $X$. Let $d_-\le d_+$ be real numbers. If a finite child $Y$ satisfies, on every $(X,Y)$ value attained in $\mathcal E$, $$d_-\le-\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf P(Y\mid X)\le d_+,
 \qquad \ell=\log(1/\epsilon),$$ then there are at most $\epsilon^{-d_+}$ retained children over each parent, and, with $\mathsf U_c=\mathsf U(\,\cdot\mid C=c)$, $$d_- -\frac{\log(1/r_C(c))}{\ell}
 \le \mathsf H^{\mathsf U_c}(Y\mid X)\le d_+.
 \label{eq:typical-cell-entropy}$$ More precisely, outside $\mathsf U_c$-mass at most $\eta_1+\eta_2$, $$d_- -\frac{\log(1/(\eta_1r_C(c)))}{\ell}
 \le-\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf U_c(Y\mid X)
 \le d_+ +\frac{\log(1/\eta_2)}{\ell},
 \qquad 0<\eta_2<1.
 \label{eq:typical-cell-surprise}$$ These conclusions concern the retained support and sampled conditional values. They assert no lower mass bound for every untrimmed child.

For any finite tag $Q$, $$\begin{aligned}
 0\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(D\mid B)-\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(D\mid B,Q)&\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(Q),\\
 |\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(T;D\mid Q)-\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(T;D)|&\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(Q),\\
 \mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(U;V\mid Z,Q)&\le\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(U;V\mid Z)+\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(Q).
\end{aligned}$$ The conditional quantities on the left are averages of the quantities on the individual tag fibers. If $U,V$ are conditionally independent given $Z$ under $\mathsf P$, and $\mathsf R\le K\mathsf P$, then $$\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}^{\mathsf R}(U;V\mid Z)\le\log K.$$ Given a joint law of $(T,C,V)$ and a kernel $\kappa(u\mid T,C)$, one may adjoin $U$ by this kernel while preserving that entire joint law. The new $U$ is conditionally independent of $V$ given $(T,C)$, and its joint law with $(T,C)$ is the prescribed kernel law.

Fix a law $\mathsf P$, a finite list $(X_j,Y_j)$, $1\le j\le q$, and numbers $A_j\ge0$ such that $|\mathcal Y_j|\le\epsilon^{-A_j}$. There is no cardinality assumption on $X_j$. For $a,\sigma,\theta>0$, there are disjoint events $E_z$ whose union has probability at least $1-q\epsilon^\sigma-\theta$, with the following properties. The number of events is at most $$J=\prod_{j=1}^q\left(1+\left\lceil\frac{A_j+\sigma}{a}\right\rceil\right), \qquad m_z:=\mathsf P(E_z)\ge\theta/J.$$ For each $z,j$ there is $d_{j,z}\in[0,A_j+\sigma]$ such that, on $E_z$, $$d_{j,z}\le -\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf P(Y_j\mid X_j) \le d_{j,z}+a. \label{eq:homogeneous-bin}$$ If $\mathsf R$ is any law supported on $E_z$ satisfying $\mathsf R\le K\mathsf P(\,\cdot\mid E_z)$, then $$d_{j,z}-\frac{\log(K/m_z)}\ell \le\mathsf H_{\mathsf R}(Y_j\mid X_j)\le d_{j,z}+a. \label{eq:homogeneous-entropy}$$ More precisely, for every $0<\eta<1$, outside a set of $\mathsf R$-probability at most $2\eta$, $$d_{j,z}-\frac{\log(K/(m_z\eta))}\ell \le-\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf R(Y_j\mid X_j) \le d_{j,z}+a+\frac{\log(1/\eta)}\ell. \label{eq:homogeneous-surprise}$$ There are at most $\epsilon^{-(d_{j,z}+a)}$ retained $Y_j$ values over each fixed $X_j$ value. The support-count assertion and [eq:homogeneous-bin] are uniform on the retained support, before any further restriction is chosen.

Let $\pi$ be a law and let $\Lambda$ be a comparison probability law with $\pi\ll\Lambda$. Write $L=d\pi/d\Lambda$ and $D=\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi\Vert\Lambda)$. For every $v>0$, $$\pi(\log L>v)\le\frac{D+1/e}{v}.
 \label{eq:likelihood-tail}$$ Consequently, if $D=o(\ell)$, there is $v=o(\ell)$ such that $\pi(\log L>v)=o(1)$, and the remaining subprobability is bounded by $e^v\Lambda$. This applies in particular to $$\Lambda(a,b,c)=\pi_C(c)\pi_{A\mid C}(a\mid c)
                            \pi_{B\mid C}(b\mid c),
 \qquad D=\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}^\pi(A;B\mid C).$$ Conversely, if a probability law $\rho$ satisfies $\rho\le K\prod_{i=1}^k\mu_i$, then $$\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}\left(\rho\middle\Vert\prod_i\rho_i\right)\le\log K.
 \label{eq:product-information}$$

       \le A_l\prod_{j=1}^{k_l}\mu_{lj},
 \label{eq:core-comparison}$$ where every $\mu_{lj}$ is a specified probability law. Put $q=\sum_l k_l$. Repeated occurrences of an observation with different comparison laws are counted separately. For $0<\eta<m/q$ there is a restriction $

Let $\pi(p,b)$ be a probability law with $\mu=\pi_P$, $\lambda=\pi_B$. Let $E$ be an allowed set with $\pi(E)\ge1-\zeta$ and suppose $$\boldsymbol1_E(p,b)\pi(p,b)\le K\mu(p)\lambda(b),\qquad K\ge1. \label{eq:pair-product}$$ Choose $0<\alpha<1$ with $\zeta<1-\alpha$, retain only point fibers with $r(p):=\pi(E\mid P=p)\ge\alpha$, and normalize the pairs in these fibers and in $E$ to a law $q$. Its retained mass $M_0$ satisfies $$M_0\ge1-\frac{\zeta}{1-\alpha},\qquad q(p,b)\le M_0^{-1}\pi(p,b),\qquad q(b\mid p)\le c\lambda(b),\quad c:=K/\alpha. \label{eq:star-kernel}$$ For a fixed integer $n\ge1$, sample $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ independently given $P$ with kernel $q(b\mid p)$, and let $$S(p,b_1,\ldots,b_n)=q_P(p)\prod_{i=1}^nq(b_i\mid p).$$ The following are comparison probability laws on the whole star: $$\begin{aligned} \Lambda_0&=q_P\otimes\lambda^{\otimes n}, &S&\le c^n\Lambda_0,\label{eq:star-independent}\\ \Lambda_i&=q_{P,B_i}\otimes\bigotimes_{j\ne i}\lambda_{B_j}, &S&\le c^{n-1}\Lambda_i\quad(1\le i\le n). \label{eq:star-pair} \end{aligned}$$ Here $q_{P,B_i}$ is a copy of the retained pair law $q$. It may be replaced by the original $\pi$ in [eq:star-pair] at the additional cost $M_0^{-1}$.* *Let $R=wS/m$, where $0\le w\le1$ and $m=\mathbb E_Sw>0$. Fix an index set $J\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of *fixed labels*; write $F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus J$ for the *free labels*. Choose any observation $$C=(B_J,Z),\qquad Z=f(P,B_J).$$ Thus the function defining $Z$ involves the point and the fixed labels only. For every $0<\eta<1/(n+1)$, there is a set of $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at least $1-(n+1)\eta$ on which, simultaneously, $$\begin{aligned} R(\,\cdot\mid C)&\le\frac{c^n}{m\eta}\Lambda_0(\,\cdot\mid C), \label{eq:conditional-independent}\\ R(\,\cdot\mid C)&\le\frac{c^{n-1}}{m\eta} \Lambda_i(\,\cdot\mid C),\quad1\le i\le n. \label{eq:conditional-pair} \end{aligned}$$ For a fixed value $C=(b_J,z)$, put $z_{b_J}(p)=f(p,b_J)$. Ignoring the deterministic coordinates $B_J$, these comparison laws are exactly $$\begin{aligned} \Lambda_0(\,\cdot\mid b_J,z) &=q_P(\,\cdot\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z) \otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F}\lambda_{B_j}, \label{eq:fixed-comparison-zero}\\ \Lambda_i(\,\cdot\mid b_J,z) &=q_P(\,\cdot\mid B_i=b_i,z_{b_J}(P)=z) \otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F}\lambda_{B_j}, &&i\in J,\label{eq:fixed-comparison-pair}\\ \Lambda_i(\,\cdot\mid b_J,z) &=q_{P,B_i}(\,\cdot\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z) \otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F\setminus\{i\}}\lambda_{B_j}, &&i\in F.\label{eq:free-comparison-pair} \end{aligned}$$ Conditionals in this display need only be defined when their conditioning event has positive comparison mass; the inequalities hold at every $R$-positive value under consideration.* *There is also a direct comparison using the actual point marginal. There is a set $G$ of $(P,C)$ values with $R(G)\ge1-\eta$ such that, for every $C$ value, as an inequality of subprobabilities, $$\boldsymbol1_G(p,C)R(p,b_F\mid C) \le\frac{c^{|F|}}{m\eta}R_P(p\mid C) \prod_{j\in F}\lambda(b_j). \label{eq:actual-point-free}$$ For $0<\tau<1$, outside $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at most $\eta/\tau$, the subprobability on the left has mass at least $1-\tau$. In any of these conditionals, all applicable product comparisons, including product comparisons for coordinate tuples at several fixed labels, may be converted *simultaneously* to comparisons using their actual retained marginals by Lemma 7. If the subprobability after all prior trims, including intersection with $G$ when used, has conditional mass $u$ and the resulting list has $N_{\mathrm{fac}}$ factor occurrences, its core has conditional mass at least $u/2$ and each $k$-factor comparison constant $A$ becomes at most $A(2N_{\mathrm{fac}}/u)^k$. All exceptional-mass and domination estimates above are independent of the number of possible values of $C$, $P$, and the labels.

Fix the values of some labels. On that fiber let $
u$ be a retained probability law of a point $P$ and free labels $(B_j)_{j\in F}$, with $$
u\le A
u_P\otimes igotimes_{j\in F}\lambda_j.$$ The comparison laws $\lambda_j$ may be the actual marginals obtained by a simultaneous core on this fiber. If $Z=f(P)$, then on every positive $Z$ fiber, $$
u(p,b_F\mid Z=z)
 \le A
u_P(p\mid Z=z)\prod_{j\in F}\lambda_j(b_j).$$ Thus the comparison label populations are those *before* the point slice, and any mass upper bounds already proved for them remain available. After a further restriction and core of conditional mass $M>0$, each new actual label marginal is bounded by $A/M$ times its respective $\lambda_j$.

The following three statements hold.*

1.  *Suppose for each $\epsilon\to0$ there is a countable list $(X_j,Y_j)_{j\ge1}$, with $|\mathcal Y_j|\le\epsilon^{-A_j}$ for each fixed $j$. One can partition all but $o(1)$ of the law into $\epsilon^{-o(1)}$ parts, each of mass at least $\epsilon^{o(1)}$, such that the following holds. From any choice of one retained part at each scale, a subsequence can be extracted on which every listed observation is homogeneous. The same exponents are inherited by every sequence of laws supported on those parts whose density relative to their normalized laws is at most $\epsilon^{-o(1)}$. The assertion is simultaneous for joint observations and observations conditional on an exact particle index, when these are included in the list.*

2.  *Let $v$ range over a compact rectangle of depth parameters. Suppose observations $Y_v$, conditional on any $X$, obey, uniformly for fixed $u,v$, the two ambiguity bounds $$\log N(Y_v\mid Y_u,X),\ \log N(Y_u\mid Y_v,X)
           \le C\ell\|u-v\|_1+o(\ell),$$ and have bounded normalized alphabet sizes at one reference depth. Their normalized entropy profiles have subsequences converging on all depths to a $C$-Lipschitz function, after extraction on a countable dense set. Homogeneous surprise exponents on that dense set extend to the same function at every fixed depth, provided the ambiguity bounds also hold on the retained support.*

3.  *Suppose a finite construction at each fixed $h>0$ has finitely many normalized errors tending to zero as $\epsilon\to0$. Given any sequence of permissible $h_k\downarrow0$, and any countable sequence of such requirements, a diagonal can be chosen so that the first $k$ requirements have errors at most $h_k/k$ and $h_k\log(1/\epsilon_k)\to\infty$. Thus errors may be made $o(h)$ before passing to the scale $\epsilon^h$. This assertion supplies no rate uniform in $h$ or in the limiting profile.

Fix $0<s\le1$, $0<d\le2$, and $\alpha>0$. There are $\eta_0=\eta_0(\alpha,s,d)>0$ and $\rho_0=\rho_0(\alpha,s,d)>0$ with the following property. Suppose $\mathcal P$ is a nonempty $(\rho,d,\rho^{-\eta_0})$-set of squares, with $0<\rho<\rho_0$. For each $p\in\mathcal P$, let $\mathcal T(p)$ be a family of tubes meeting $p$, of cardinality comparable to $M$, and forming a $(\rho,s,\rho^{-\eta_0})$-set. Then $$\#\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathcal T(p)
 \gtrsim_\alpha
 \rho^{-\min\{1,d,(d+s)/2\}+\alpha}M .
 \label{eq:ren-wang-discrete}$$ The statement is unchanged by fixed bounded domains, finitely many coordinate charts, or fixed-factor enlargements of the grids and tubes, after decreasing $\eta_0,\rho_0$ if necessary.

Fix $0<d\le2$, $0<s\le1$, and $\alpha>0$, and fixed bounded point and slope domains. There are $\eta>0$ and $\rho_1>0$ such that the following holds for $0<\rho<\rho_1$. Let $\mu$ be a finite probability population of points in $\mathbb R^2$. Let $\nu$ be a finite probability population of tags $b$, with a slope $a(b)$ assigned to each tag. Suppose $$\begin{aligned}
 \mu(B(z,r))&\le \rho^{-\eta}r^d,
 & (a_*\nu)(I)&\le \rho^{-\eta}r^s
 \label{eq:projection-populations}

Suppose an incidence population uses at most $N$ point cells. Let $E$ be a set of occupied $\rho$-cells in a fixed bounded region.*


1.  *In $\mathbb R^3$, let $v_1,v_2,v_3\in\mathbb R^2$ be bounded slopes and put $D=\abs{\det((1,v_1),(1,v_2),(1,v_3))}>0$. If $\pi_{v_i}(E)$ uses at most $N_i$ cells, with bounded enlargements permitted, then $$\abs E^2\leq C D^{-6}N_1N_2N_3.
     \label{eq:isotropic-lw}$$*


2.  *In $\mathbb R^2$, for two bounded scalar slopes $v_1,v_2$ with $\abs{v_1-v_2}\geq\rho^a$, if their intercepts use at most $N_1,N_2$ cells, then $$\abs E\leq C\rho^{-2a}N_1N_2.
     \label{eq:isotropic-two-projections}$$

Let $b$ be Lipschitz on an interval $J$, and let $\Gamma=\{(b(u),u):u\in J\}$ lie in an open plane region. Suppose bounded fields $a_j,D$ in this region satisfy $V_ja_j\in\mathcal M_{\rm loc}$ and $\partial_iD\in\mathcal M_{\rm loc}$, where $\mathcal M_{\rm loc}$ denotes locally finite signed measures. Put $p(u)=-b'(u)$ at points where this derivative exists. For almost every $u\in J$ the field $D$ has two strong traces $D^-,D^+$ and every $a_j$ with $c_j\ne p(u)$ has two strong traces $a_j^-,a_j^+$. Specifically, at $q_0=(b(u_0),u_0)$ the mean of $|a_j-a_j^\pm(u_0)|$ tends to zero on the corresponding tangent half-ball $$B_\rho(q_0)\cap
 \{\ \pm(i-b(u_0)+p(u_0)(u-u_0))>0\ \},
 \qquad\rho\downarrow0,$$ and likewise for $D$. The same assertion holds with the actual sides $\pm(i-b(u))>0$. No assertion is made about the field whose speed equals $p(u_0)$.*


*If, in addition, $V_na_n\ge\partial_iD$, then at almost every transverse point $p\ne c_n$, $$\label{eq:trace-curve-jump}
 D^- -D^+\ge(c_n-p)(a_n^+-a_n^-).$$ These conclusions apply to curves on the boundary of an aperture region whenever the fields are defined in an ambient neighborhood; one then retains only the side lying in that region.

For almost every point $(i,u)$ of the characteristic plane with $i>0$ and $0<u<1$, put $s=S'(u)$. There is a constant $\sigma>0$, depending only on the matched process and $m$, for which $0<s\le1$ and the following assertions hold.*

1.  *If $m\ne1$, each of the chains $x\longrightarrow y$ and $w\longrightarrow z$ has the rule $$d>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad e\ge\min(1,d+s),$$ where $d,e$ are its source and target rates. Each of $x\longrightarrow w$ and $y\longrightarrow z$ has the same rule with $\sigma$ in place of $s$.*

     z<1\Longrightarrow q\le2-s.$$*

*The bounds include $0\le x,y,w,z\le1$, or $0\le q\le2$ in the tied case, supplied by the coordinate capacities.

Fix an integer $k\ge1$. Let $p^0$ be a probability law on a finite pair space $\mathcal P\times\Theta$. Write $\mu^0=p^0_P$ and $\lambda^0=p^0_\theta$. Define the two nonnegative natural-log quantities $$\begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{pair}}
 &=\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(p^0_{P,\theta}\Vert\mu^0\otimes\lambda^0),\\
 D_{\mathrm{coord}}
 &=\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}\left(p^0_{\theta,Q_1,\ldots,Q_k}
       \middle\Vert
       \lambda^0(\theta)\prod_{j=1}^k\xi_j^\theta(Q_j)\right)\\

       -\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\mid\theta).

*Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite list of observations on the pair space which contains $P$, $\theta$, and every $(\theta,Q_j)$. It may also contain any finite list of prefix and joint observations.  \le1-\zeta-\frac{D_{\mathrm{pair}}+D_{\mathrm{coord}}+2/e}{v},

 \label{eq:block-core-floors}$$ For the normalized law $\pi=r/M$, write $\mu=\pi_P$ and $\lambda=\pi_\theta$. Its pair law and its coordinate law on every positive label fiber satisfy $$\begin{aligned}

 \label{eq:block-core-pair}\\

          \prod_{j=1}^k\pi(Q_j\mid\theta).

\end{aligned}$$ All factors on the right of these two inequalities are marginals of this same law $\pi$.*


*If $A,B$ are listed observations and $A$ is determined by $B$, then for every retained child value $b$, with parent $a=A(b)$, $$\delta p^0(B=b\mid A=a)
 \le \pi(B=b\mid A=a)
 \le\delta^{-1}p^0(B=b\mid A=a).
 \label{eq:block-core-prefix-ratio}$$ The upper inequality can be summed over any set of child values. The lower inequality is asserted only for retained children. In particular, fix $0<\rho<1$. If on $\mathcal H$ the original conditional surprises for this pair lie in $[d_-,d_+]$ in units $L=\log(1/\rho)$, then every retained parent has at most $\rho^{-d_+}$ retained children, and its retained conditional child masses obey $$\delta\rho^{d_+}
 \le\pi(B=b\mid A=a)\le\delta^{-1}\rho^{d_-}.$$ When a parent is nested only up to bounded ambiguity, include it in the child symbol before applying this assertion.

 \label{eq:packet-coeff-canonical}$$ with a fixed constant.*

*More quantitatively, choose $0<\eta<\Delta/4$ and any required power $A>0$. There are an integer integration order $M$, a coefficient cutoff exponent $B$, constants $C_A$, and $\epsilon_0>0$, depending only on these choices and the fixed data, such that, for $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$:*

In a geometric localizer, bin nonnegligible coefficients so that $$|\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(|c_T|^2\right)-\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)|\le\xi \label{eq:packet-mass-bin}$$ on each bin. If $N_{\rm all}$ is the full class size, then for every allowed local root cap $F$, $$\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\#\{T\hbox{ in the class}:T\in F\}\right)+w(F) \le g+e_{\rm pkt}. \label{eq:packet-cap-count}$$ An empty count imposes no restriction. The supremum $\beta_{\mathrm q}$ is finite and $\beta_{\mathrm q}\le1$. This conclusion uses no identification of the original coherent mass with a positive particle law.
